messages:
carla: FYI I'm seeing a burst of 429s for a batch of customer keys starting ~1934567000. Dashboards show org-level quotas intact but per-key bursts dropping to 0. Rolling outage for a handful of high-throughput customers.
ben: looking. Any recent console changes or config rollouts?
carla: Yes — this morning we pushed a UI change to the 'burst priority' toggle in the quota editor (console commit c4b2a1). It was supposed to default to 'preserve org priority' but I think the checkbox flipped semantics.
alice: I can repro locally: the API records burst_policy.priority = "token" and token_priority = 0 (lowest) for keys that used to be high priority. Background ingestion jobs then grab burst tokens first.
ben: that explains it. So expensive background workers are draining per-key burst budgets, leaving customer requests throttled. Do we have a config snapshot?
dave: grabbing latest from config-service: `GET /configs/orgs/active?commit=c4b2a1` returns 200. Snippet: ```json
{"org_id":"org-42","keys":[{"key":"k_abc","burst":"enabled","token_priority":0}]}```
ben: Oof. token_priority should be 100 for prod customer keys. That commit set default to 0 when checkbox unchecked. Was the checkbox label ambiguous?
carla: UX used 'Use global priority' but in the backend that maps inverted. I missed the invert in the translation layer.
dave: mitigation options: 1) rollback console commit c4b2a1 (fast), 2) hotpatch config-service to invert mapping (faster?), 3) manual edit per-org keys (slow).
ben: rollbacks are safe here. Deploy-bot, can we revert c4b2a1 to previous deployment?
deploy-bot: revert pipeline triggered for commit c4b2a1 -> will deploy c3f9d8 (previous). ETA ~5m for deploy + config propagation. :hourglass:
carla: while deploys, we should throttle background ingestion to avoid further drainage. alice can you flip worker feature-flag?
alice: flipping ff_ingest_high_throughput -> off for prod. Command: `kubectl set env deploy/ingest FF_INGEST_HIGH_THROUGHPUT=false -n prod` — done. Workers should slow in ~30s.
ben: monitoring: adding temporary rule to alert if per-key burst remaining < 5% for any key with traffic > 100 qps.
oncall: Incident created INC-2026-193456. Notifying oncall rotation.
dave: after revert finished, config-service shows token_priority back to 100 for affected keys. Sample: ```json
{"key":"k_abc","token_priority":100}```
carla: customers reporting reduced 429s. Good catch team.
ben: postmortem notes: console UX inversion bug + missing unit test for mapping + no guard in config-service for token_priority out-of-range. Action items: 1) add unit test in console for mapping semantics, 2) add server-side validation rejecting token_priority < 1 for customer keys, 3) add rollout safety check in console 'apply to multiple orgs' flows, 4) add a dashboard for token-priority drift.
alice: I'll open PRs for 1 & 2.
dave: I'll add a CI check for console commit that ensures mapping stability.
carla: I'll draft postmortem and customer comms.
ben: marking incident resolved after monitoring for 1hr no regression. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
carla: follow-up: let's schedule an on-call runbook entry for 'burst budget unexpected drain' and CLI for emergency per-key top-up.
ben: noted. Closing thread in 1h unless new alerts.
